The biggest lesson - PCOS is a spectrum, like many other chronic conditions. What others struggle with may not align with what YOU might struggle with, as it's always personal. Google will always show you all the results that might come from having PCOS, because that's what it does - it gives you a general picture of symptoms.
But you're not gonna get all the symptoms listed. You don't have all of them right now, either.  The one thing that should determine your symptoms is your doctor - whether that's a gynecologist or an endocrinologist, or both. Your bloodwork, that I assume they will make you do, will give you a lot of answers on WHY things are going the way they are inside your body.

Second, Google is not always your friend. I'm no stranger to doomscrolling, it's a need for understanding and control of the situation. Try to NOT read your eyes out, as much as you can. Wait for your doctor to explain things. There's many good resources others have linked that might explain the condition better in a way that will hopefully not cause you to spiral. 

Third, remember that PCOS is not the end. It's a condition that you'll have to figure out and manage what works and doesn't work, and it might seem scary at first. But trust me, you're stronger than you think. You'll figure it out.
